evals.name: three-derived-repos
evals.prompt: J'ai un repo de base ~/work/base-template et trois projets dérivés ~/work/service-a, ~/work/service-b, ~/work/service-c. Ils doivent tous suivre exactement le même workflow. Vérifie qu'il n'y a pas de dérive et dis-moi quoi corriger.
evals.expected_output: A drift matrix across the three projects, differences classified (stale copy, local improvement, intentional override, defect, unknown) using git history, repeated differences grouped, a recommendation for a mechanism that removes the cause, and nothing modified or deleted.
expectations: A file-level comparison of the base against every derived project is produced (for example with scripts/drift_matrix.py)
Paths are sorted into must-match, parametrised and local-only before verdicts are given
Each difference is classified with evidence from git history rather than guessed
A difference with no evidence either way is reported as unknown and put to the user
Differences that repeat across projects are grouped into one finding
A prevention mechanism is recommended (reusable workflow, template update tool or CI drift check), not only a one-off sync
No file in any repository is modified or deleted

evals.name: copy-pasted-ci
evals.prompt: Le workflow CI a été copié-collé dans 12 repos et personne ne sait lesquels sont à jour. Comment on règle ça pour de bon ?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to reference the workflow rather than copy it (reusable workflow pinned to a commit SHA, or a template-update tool), a CI check that fails on drift, and a note on what stays parametrised.
expectations: Referencing a single definition (reusable workflow or equivalent) is recommended over repeated manual syncing
Pinning the reference to a commit SHA or release tag is mentioned
A CI check or scheduled audit that detects drift is proposed
The answer separates what must be identical from what is parametrised per repository
